subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: After rejected writes are made atomic, should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` fail closed on every legacy ownerless row despite the upgrade compatibility break?
rationale: Code inspection can establish safe enforcement mechanics, but maintainers must choose the trust and recovery policy for rows created before plugin ownership metadata existed.

options.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
options.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches and require operator or non-plugin management for legacy ownerless sessions.

options.title: Add an explicit migration path
options.body: Provide a doctor or ownership-assignment recovery flow before enforcing the denial.

options.title: Preserve legacy access temporarily
options.body: Allow a documented transition window while accepting a weaker plugin-isolation boundary.

recommendation.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
recommendation.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches and require operator or non-plugin management for legacy ownerless sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across the session handler, archive lifecycle, and plugin-runtime dispatch surfaces and are already subscribed to the PR.
